subject: Clarify default capture + deletion behavior for streaming / KV cache
messages:
From: Anna L. Sorensen <anna@fjordhealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Default log retention — streaming requests, KV cache, and delete API?

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. We're wrapping up procurement for a pilot and need a clear answer on Redwood's default capture and deletion behavior so we can get legal sign-off. A few concrete questions below — short bullets are great.

1) What is the default retention window for hosted API requests/responses (prompts vs model outputs)? Are prompts treated differently from outputs?
2) For streaming sessions (server-sent chunks / partial outputs), are those segments stored after the session? If so, how long and for what purpose (e.g., debugging vs billing)?
3) How does KV cache (chat history / prefix caching) persist across sessions — is any of that written to durable storage?
4) Is there a deletion API for customers to request immediate erasure? If yes, what is the SLA (how long until data is removed everywhere, including backups)?
5) Any difference in behavior for EU residency customers (data kept inside EU vs global backups)?
6) Do outputs that contain PHI/PII follow a different workflow?

We have regulatory constraints (HIPAA-adjacent) so the procurement and infosec teams need language we can include in the DPA.

Thanks — Anna
Anna Sorensen
Head of Security, Fjord Health

[Attachment: procurement_retention_questions.docx (docx)]
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Anna L. Sorensen <anna@fjordhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Default log retention — streaming requests, KV cache, and delete API?

Anna — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers + pointers; I'll follow up with a short attestation draft for procurement and loop Legal if you want a signature.

High-level summary (hosted API defaults):
- Default capture window: raw request (input) and model response (output) are retained for 30 days by default. This is used for observability, billing reconciliation, quality monitoring, and safety/regression alerts.
- Prompts vs outputs: we classify the original user prompt as an input artifact and model-generated text as an output artifact; both are captured by default and share the same 30-day retention policy unless a customer enables no-capture.
- Streaming segments: transient streaming chunks are kept only for the active session and are not persisted to long-term logs by default. For debugging/incident investigation we keep a short diagnostic trail (non-production traces) for up to 48 hours, then purge.
- KV cache/chat history: KV caches used for live inference are in-memory by design. They are written to durable storage only when a customer opts into session export or long-running conversation persistence; otherwise they are ephemeral to the session and discarded at session end.
- Deletion API: yes — we provide a deletion endpoint (DELETE /v1/customers/:id/data-requests) that returns a request_id you can track. Typical processing: 0–24 hours to remove primary copies, up to 72 hours to remove copies from backups/secondary stores. We provide the request_id and completion events via webhook.
- EU residency: customers can restrict hosted artifacts to EU regions. Data residence constrains primary storage to the chosen region; backups may be geo-redundant within the same EU boundary if configured. Cross-border transfer only occurs with explicit customer opt-in or for legal reasons.
- PHI/PII: we don't treat outputs differently by type automatically — customers with PHI requirements should enable Private deployment or Dedicated with the appropriate controls. For hosted customers, we offer a HIPAA addendum and additional controls (KMS integration, restricted retention) — we will provide templated addenda for procurement.

Attachments + links:
- retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (attached) — matrix of artifact types, default retention, and purge timelines.
- retention_playbook_excerpt.pdf (attached) — excerpt of deletion workflow and API examples.
- Support ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/RI-4589 (I opened a ticket to track the formal attestation).

A few caveats and next steps:
- The 30-day default is for our hosted offering; Dedicated and Private deployments are configurable per contract and can be set to shorter windows or customer-managed deletion timelines.
- Deletion SLA language in DPAs is negotiable for enterprise customers; procurement often asks for a 72-hour backup purge guarantee — we can include that in an enterprise addendum.

If you'd like, I can:
- Draft a 1-page attestation of current behavior for procurement to attach to the SOW.
- Start a Legal loop to produce a HIPAA/retention addendum.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify default capture + deletion behavior for streaming / KV cache

Hannah — helpful summary, thanks. A couple follow-ups so we can close our questionnaire: 

- Does the deletion API provide a formal confirmation or certificate of deletion we can attach to the DPA? Our procurement needs a time-bound artifact.
- Are embeddings/derived artifacts treated the same as raw outputs? We generate embeddings server-side for reranking and want to be sure those are purged on request.
- For the 48–72 hour backup purge window you mentioned, is there a mechanism to escalate for faster removal if required by regulation?

Also — can you confirm whether the EU residency option prevents any logs from ever leaving the EU (including for logs created during deploy/incident response)?

If it's easier, happy to have a short call tomorrow with Karthik and Kimberly to get wording locked.

— Anna
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Anna L. Sorensen <anna@fjordhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify default capture + deletion behavior for streaming / KV cache

Anna — quick confirmations inline and next steps.

- Certificate / proof of deletion: the deletion API issues a request_id and we record a completion event with a signed timestamped attestation (PDF) that can be attached to contracts. We'll include that artifact in the attestation I'm drafting (and attach to ticket RI-4589).
- Embeddings / derived artifacts: treated as derived outputs and covered by the same deletion request. When a deletion request is processed we purge raw inputs, model outputs, and derived artifacts (embeddings, reranking vectors) from primary stores and mark them for backup purge.
- Faster removal: for enterprise customers (Dedicated/Private) we can offer an accelerated remediation SLA as part of the contract. For hosted customers, we provide an escalation path through our Support + Trust teams — we can commit to triage and a documented escalation window but wholesale backup rekeying/irreversible removal may still take time depending on storage layers.
- EU residency: when configured for EU-only residency with the region lock option, primary copies and geo-redundant backups are constrained to EU regions. Incident-response access is similarly scoped, and cross-border transfer only occurs under legal compulsion or explicit customer opt-in. We'll include the exact region-lock verbiage in the attestation.

Next steps I will take today:
1) Attach retention_matrix_v2.xlsx and the playbook excerpt to support ticket RI-4589.
2) Draft a 1-page signed attestation + sample DPA clause for your procurement team (ETA: EOD Friday).
3) Offer a 30-minute call Friday at 11am ET with Karthik and Kimberly to finalize wording if that helps.

If that timeline works I'll send calendar invite and attach the draft attestation.

Best,
Hannah
Director, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
